disabled_the_energy_storage: When enabled: System automatically charges battery to reserve level from solar and grid whenever power is low, during normal operation or after power outages. When disabled: after the power outage was restored,, system charges battery from solar only, not from grid.
dynamic_tariff_scheduling_tip: The electricity price we obtain from EPEX or other public channels is the <highlight>market price</highlight>, which is the transaction price of electricity in the market and usually changes with demand and supply. However, please note that the price on your electricity bill is usually the <highlight>settlement price</highlight>, which includes additional fees such as transportation fees, distribution fees, and taxes and may be significantly different from the market price. Therefore, when you optimize the charging and discharging time of energy storage system in AlphaESS based on the dynamic market price, we recommend that you take this difference into account and check the actual settlement price with your electricity supplier. This helps you make the optimal energy storage decision.

germany_dynamic_elec_price_tip2: When the dynamic tariff function is enabled, the energy storage system may, under certain operating conditions, feed electricity back into the public grid.
germany_dynamic_elec_price_tip3: Depending on the country/region, local regulations, DSO (Distribution System Operator) rules, and individual commercial or residential energy contracts, such feed-in may be restricted or prohibited.
germany_dynamic_elec_price_tip4: Therefore, the customer is solely responsible for verifying that:
germany_dynamic_elec_price_tip5: Their electricity supply / dynamic tariff contract allows feeding back electricity that was previously purchased from the public grid;
germany_dynamic_elec_price_tip6: Any additional metering, permits, or market participation requirements (e.g., direct marketing obligations) have been met;
germany_dynamic_elec_price_tip7: All legal, contractual, and financial consequences of enabling this feature are borne by the customer.
germany_elec_price_setting_tip10: Please ensure that all parameters are entered accurately according to your actual electricity contract and billing information. AlphaESS shall not be held liable for any miscalculations, system malfunctions, or financial losses resulting from incorrect or improper data entry by the user.
germany_elec_price_setting_tip2: The EPEX spot price is quoted as a net price (excluding VAT). Therefore, the standard conversion coefficient is 1.19 (19% VAT). However, please refer to your electricity contract: if your contract includes a percentage-based adjustment on EPEX, this adjustment must first be applied and then multiplied by 1.19 to obtain the final coefficient.By correctly setting this coefficient, we can optimize the charging and discharging of your energy storage system based on your actual expenditure and electricity price, ensuring maximum benefits for you.
germany_elec_price_setting_tip4: In a dynamic electricity contract, the total price typically consists of three components:
germany_elec_price_setting_tip7: 3. Additional costs such as grid usage fees (Netznutzungsentgelte), retail markups (Vertriebskostenaufschlag), taxes, levies, surcharges, and green energy certificates.
germany_elec_price_setting_tip8: For system configuration, we recommend that you enter the costs related to Netznutzungsentgelte, taxes, levies, surcharges, and renewable energy certificates.The total of these items is referred to as the surcharge. Entering this data allows the system to calculate your actual electricity costs correctly and helps you achieve greater savings.
germany_elec_price_setting_tip9: Please always refer to your actual electricity bill, as Vertriebskostenaufschlag and Netznutzungsentgelte vary depending on your supplier and region.

high_price_tooltip: The data points within this interval represent periods of high electricity prices. The proportion of time in a day classified as “high price” is based on the set percentage of the total data packets. Every day, the system retrieves electricity price data from the market and sorts it from low to high. For example, if the high-price threshold is set to 70%, the system calculates 96 data packets × 70% to determine the number of high-price hours. The result is rounded to the nearest whole number and marked with a red line. After fetching the next day’s market prices, the system automatically recalculates the high-price threshold interval.
home_work_mode_tip: The Self-Consumption mode is the default mode of operation of the system, and the system will run automatically when other modes are not enabled.
how_works_desc: Automatically manages your battery to reduce electricity costs.
in_window_tip_2: Stops at the daily cap, Max SOC, or window end.
in_window_tip_3: Pauses for VPP, Storm Guard, or Force; resumes if still in window.
low_price_tooltip: The data points within this interval represent periods of low electricity prices. The proportion of time in a day classified as “low price” is based on the set percentage of the total data packets. Every day, the system retrieves electricity price data from the market and sorts it from low to high. For example, if the low-price threshold is set to 30%, the system calculates 96 data packets × 30% to determine the number of low-price hours. The result is rounded to the nearest whole number and marked with a green line. After fetching the next day’s market prices, the system automatically recalculates the low-price threshold interval.
max_solar_consumption: Priority is given to photovoltaic power supply, and the remaining power is used to charge the battery, and then draw power from the grid when the power is insufficient.
neg_electricity_price_dispatch_tip: To comply with the provisions effective from March 2025 in Germany, the Energy Industry Act (EnWG) Amendment 2025, AlphaESS integrates historical solar data, weather forecasts, and other relevant information to intelligently predict power generation during periods of negative electricity tariffs. Before the anticipated negative tariff periods, the system will automatically adjust the battery charging and discharging strategy, releasing some stored energy in advance to reduce the risk of feeding energy into the grid. Please note that the forecast data is for reference only, and actual power generation may deviate due to weather, device status, and other factors, which could still result in grid feed-in during negative tariff periods. We recommend that users monitor system data in real time and decide whether to enable this feature based on their actual usage to achieve more efficient energy management. Please note that this regulation only applies to users from March 2025 onwards. Before enabling this feature, please confirm that you are within the applicable scope. When enabled, this feature's energy scheduling strategy will take precedence over the custom scheduling strategy based on dynamic tariffs.
negative_price_basis_desc: Based on your final buy and sell prices, including your coefficient and surcharges - not the raw market price.

off_grid_cutoff_soc: In off-grid mode, stop discharging when the SOC is discharged to the end of the SOC. The default value is 20%, and the value range is 5%~95%, and once the grid-connected mode is switched, the logic is invalid.
off_grid_soc_control_tip: In off-grid mode, when this function is enabled, the battery will be charged and discharged through the SOC value, and it will be used with the off-grid wake-up SOC and off-grid cut-off SOC.
off_grid_soc_value_tip: The current off-grid wake-up SOC setting is invalid if it is < off-grid cut-off SOC + 5%.
off_grid_wake_up_soc_tip: In off-grid mode, when the SOC is charged to the wake SOC, the closed backup side relay is triggered to restore the output. The default value is 25%, and the value range is 10%~100%. And the off-grid wake-up SOC ≥ (off-grid cut-off SOC +5%) to prevent repeated switching. Once the grid-connected mode is switched, the logic is invalid.
